text: Meridian Steel Fabricators, ticket forty-seven-seventy-one. A GL analyst tried to bulk-load three hundred journal lines using the GL journal FBDI template. Load Interface File for Import failed immediately — nothing loaded at all. High severity.

Quick refresher on the pipeline: fill in the FBDI template, it generates a data file, you upload the zipped file, Load Interface File for Import loads it into the relevant interface table, and a separate import process moves it into the application. A failure can happen at the load step, because the file itself is malformed, or at the import step, where the data loaded fine but failed application validation — that's the EF04 kind of error from lesson seventeen. This one failed at the load step, before import even started.

Reading the actual error: unexpected column structure, the file doesn't match the expected template layout. Comparing the uploaded file against a fresh copy of the template finds it: the analyst deleted a column they assumed was unnecessary, rather than just leaving it blank. Deleting or reordering columns breaks the fixed positional structure the load process depends on. Leaving a column blank is fine. Removing it is not.

That one deleted column is why the entire file failed before any of the three hundred lines could even be evaluated individually — this is a structural failure, not a content failure. The fix: start from a fresh, unmodified copy of the correct template, leave any genuinely unused columns blank, repopulate the data, and re-upload.

Resolution note: name the exact mistake — a deleted column, not a data error — and recommend a short reminder that FBDI template columns get left blank, never deleted or reordered. Up next, lesson twenty-seven: a similar kind of upload, through ADFdi instead of FBDI.
